Issued at 139 PM CDT Tue Sep 8 2026

This Afternoon - Overnight: Additional Showers and Storms, Some 
Strong to Severe Possible 

Showers and storms this morning have gradually exited the 
region with an initial axis of 850mb moisture transport that is 
interacting with the slowly eastward progressing front and was
responsible for much of the showers/storms this morning. As we 
head into the evening, a secondary axis of 850mb moisture 
transport related to the increasing nocturnal low-level jet will
aid in reinvigorating convective development by late afternoon 
through the overnight. Overall, the environment looks somewhat 
favorable for severe weather with hodograph presentation due to
favorable mid-level shear being present in RAP soundings across
northeast IA. This combined with initial MUCAPE values of 
around 2000 J/kg would support the potential for some initial 
discrete supercells before clustering into a multi- 
cellular/linear complex as this moisture transport overrides the
front. As a result, thinking there is a brief window for some 
severe hail before damaging wind gusts would be the primary 
threat. One important caveat to note though is that the severe 
potential in the local area is also contingent on exactly how
this moisture transport axis orients itself which may remain to
our south by evening and thus keeping most of the convection to
our south.

Heavy rainfall will be a possibility as well with the moisture 
transport overriding the boundary allowing for storms to develop on 
the front with precipitable waters also approaching 2 inches. 
Additionally, warm cloud depths remain around 4km so overall a 
fairly favorable environment for heavy rainfall. Currently, the 
recent HREF has some higher probabilities (30-60%) for rainfall 
amounts over 1 inch across northeast IA with the 90th percentile 
amounts in the HREF suggesting some 2-3" amounts cannot be ruled 
out. However, this again comes with the caveat that there remains 
some uncertainty on the exact location of where the 850mb
moisture transport will set up this evening, so there is a 
scenario where the bulk of convection remains to our south. One 
additional scenario that a few of the CAMs depict as well is 
additional convection developing with the actual synoptic front 
pushing through the local area, not associated with the 850mb 
moisture transport axis. Overall confidence in this scenario is 
somewhat low as it is unclear if enough instability will be 
present due to being clouded over for much of the daytime and 
the main moisture plume remaining to the south. Regardless, 
would expect convection to exit the region by early Wednesday 
morning as the synoptic front passes through. 

Wednesday - Thursday: Drier, Near-Normal Temperatures 

As we head into Wednesday and Thursday, upper-level ridging and 
surface high pressure build into the region. Consequently, 
expecting fairly dry conditions during this period. With some 
northwesterly flow into Thursday, expecting a slight dip in 
temperatures with highs in the middle 70s to near 80. However, 
even though the cold front passed through the local area 
Wednesday morning, temperatures will still remain near-normal 
due to upper-level ridging being in place. 

Friday - This Weekend: Shower/Storm Chances Return, Slight Cool Down

By the time we reach Friday and the weekend, precipitation 
chances will be on the increase as an upper-level trough and 
attending surface cold front pushes through the Upper Midwest 
later Friday and into Saturday morning. As a result, the grand 
ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian) has fairly high probabilities 
(75-95%) for measurable precipitation Friday night and into 
early Saturday morning. The severe potential for this period 
remains somewhat questionable as the timing of the wave would 
favor convection reaching into the local area after dark when 
instability would be waning. Consequently, much of the AI/ML 
severe outlook guidance keeps our severe potential to the west 
of the local area as the timing of the wave would need to be 
slightly faster to push the probabilities eastward. Otherwise, 
temperatures cool down past Saturday with highs potentially 
falling into the 60s to lower 70s across the area as 
northwesterly flow reinstates itself across the region. Some 
guidance would suggest a wave that pushes through northern WI on
Sunday bringing the potential for rain back into the region, so
thinking that the medium probabilities (30-50%) are feasible in
the NBM for Sunday.
